lesson.title: Review Day: Measuring Length, Time, and Money
lesson.subject: math

contentBlocks.text: This week you measured three very different things: length, time, and money. Let's review it all!

Quick review: a ruler measures length starting at the zero mark (Day 1). A clock's long hand shows minutes, counted by 5s (Day 2). Coins are counted largest-first: quarter=25, dime=10, nickel=5, penny=1 (Day 3). Money word problems ask if you have enough, or how much change you get back (Day 4). Try one of each: measure any real object with a ruler, tell what time it is on a real or drawn clock, and count 1 quarter + 1 dime + 2 pennies.
Great work this week! You practiced three real-world measurement skills: length, time, and money. Next week we'll build on these skills with something new.

objectives: Review measuring length with a ruler, telling time to the nearest 5 minutes, and counting coins
Apply all three skills to one new example each
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Do the quick walk-through review of all 4 days together, out loud.
2. Have the child measure a real object, tell a real or drawn time, and count a new coin group.
3. Complete the review worksheet.
4. Celebrate finishing a full week of real-world measurement!
differentiationTips: Struggling: focus on just the skill the child found hardest this week (often making change) rather than requiring all three equally
Ready for more: ask the child to invent their own word problem combining two of the week's skills, like timing how long it takes to count a group of coins
This is a good checkpoint to note which of the three measurement types (length, time, money) needs the most reinforcement going forward
teacherGuide.answerKey: 1 quarter + 1 dime + 2 pennies = 25 + 10 + 2 = 37 cents. Length and time answers vary based on the real object/clock used — check for correct ruler starting point and correct 5-minute reading.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Consolidates this week's three Common Core Grade 2 Measurement & Data standards (2.MD.1 length, 2.MD.7 time, 2.MD.8 money) before the course continues, matching the established Day-5-review pacing used across every unit this session.
